name: Maine
source: Maine reader session (Stage 5 tools), 2026-11-20: the November 2026 Open States dump converted with scripts/stage5/openstates/ (128th to 132nd Legislature); every House and Senate floor roll call of a 130-bill dry batch (the LD bills of 2017-2026 one topic's scan found; 7 roll calls) read from the Legislature's own roll-call PDFs, and each member's vote compared with the dump. No bill text was measured. Extended 2026-11-21: the Senate's member lists of the 128th to 132nd saved in the repo (backend/src/lib/maineLegislatureMembers.ts), the 128th to 130th House read by surname against our Open States roster of each Legislature, and the same dry batch read and compared again (95 floor roll calls). Extended again 2026-11-21: the 129th Senate read (its list and PDFs), the 130th Senate's PDF layout read, every 128th and 130th Senate row that links only a /LawMakerWeb page counted as not read, names the House PDFs print that Open States lacks added to the House roster from the House's own member profiles, and the same dry batch read and compared again (101 floor roll calls).
sessions: The Legislature is numbered and sits for two years: the 132nd is 2025-2026, with a First Regular Session in the odd year and a Second Regular Session in the even year, and special sessions as called. Bills are Legislative Documents numbered LD 1 up through the whole Legislature, and each also has a paper number by the chamber it starts in (HP 1491, SP 12). House 151 seats plus three non-voting tribal representatives; Senate 35.
bill_data: No LegiScan dataset is on disk for Maine. Bills, sponsors and roll calls come from Open States data, converted to the same folder layout (ME-900172 to ME-900176: the 128th to the 132nd Legislature, 2017-2026; scripts/stage5/openstates/README.md). Each folder carries a .openstates.json; its ids are ours and no legiscan.com page exists for them.

No Maine dump vote is placed (record_is_the_floor). The dump names House members by a label ("FAIRCLOTH of Bangor") and links some to the wrong person ("MILLETT of Waterford" on 1,162 votes to the Cape Elizabeth member), and every one of its bill and vote addresses is a /LawMakerWeb/ page, which robots.txt disallows. scripts/stage5/openstates/fetch-legislature-rollcalls.ts reads each scanned LD's House roll-call list (/house/Documents/RollCalls, by LD and Legislature) and Senate list (/<132nd>-roll-calls), keeps a row whose motion is a vote on the bill, names the Majority report, or prints none, and reads that roll call's PDF. Each list's printed count of roll calls and PDF files must equal the rows read. A row with no motion typed is read; the PDF's question decides.

Compared 2026-11-20: 7 floor roll calls read from the record (131st House 5; 132nd House 1, Senate 1). Votes on a motion skipped from the lists: 131st 45 (28 to accept a committee report), 132nd 74 (52); 3 more were read and refused as motions by the PDF's question (Refer the Bill to the Committee on Judiciary, 132nd Senate). 6 Senate floor votes of the 131st were not read: the Senate's site shows only the 132nd's member list. All 7 have a dump copy; 2 were settled by the tally among two on one day, and one day (131st LD 2224, House roll call 516) holds two dump copies with the same tally (73-66), left unsettled. Tally differences: 0. Member votes compared: 786, differences: 0 (3 labels fit two members of one family who voted alike; "BOYER of Poland" was paired by elimination).

Majority reports, 2026-11-20 (runner: "read majority report votes for Maine", "Both, with the flag"): the same dry batch read again with the vote to accept the Majority report counted as a vote on the bill. Floor roll calls read: 57 (131st House 14; 132nd 43), up from 7. 50 are Majority report votes: 30 Ought Not to Pass, 20 Ought to Pass (as amended or not). Every record Yea or Nay by a roster member (5,311) became a pair and a line, and 5,311 of 5,311 agree with the finding; 2,687 of them are on an Ought Not to Pass report and carry against_bill. Of the 40 bills whose only votes had been motions, 28 now have a floor vote read; the other 12 went by a Minority or lettered report, a referral or a tabling, or have only 131st Senate votes. Refused by the PDF: 3 Senate referrals (correct), and 132nd Senate roll call 517 (LD 1174), whose PDF prints no tally.

Roster legislators: 188 (151 Representatives, 35 Senators, 2 Tribal Representatives seated). 186 are linked: 185 by their Open States id and Aaron Dana by name. 2 are excused (no person record in the 132nd dataset): Brian Reynolds (Tribal Representative) and Nancy J. Theriault. The House PDF prints "Bridgeo, W.R." where the dump says "Bill Bridgeo", so the converter kept 18 such labels as name-only records; link_check.py links a label of that shape to the one member of its chamber whose family name it is and whose first given name starts with its first initial. Open States holds Senator Susan Bernard twice (her House-era person and her Senate one, same member email): the Senate record resolves to the House-era id, linked by hand in idmap.tsv. Every record Yea or Nay by a roster member (709) became a pair; the line tool wrote 709 lines.

Senate lists and the 128th-130th House, 2026-11-21: the same dry batch read again. Floor roll calls read: 95, up from 57 (128th House 5; 129th House 6; 130th House 10; 131st House 14, Senate 17; 132nd House 22, Senate 21). The 132nd read the same 43 with the live senators page no longer fetched. Of the 131st's 6 Senate votes skipped before (no member list), 5 now read and roll call 119 is refused as an amendment motion (correct). Refused by the PDF: the same 4 in the 132nd (3 referrals, roll call 517 with no tally). Not read: 3 House roll calls of the 128th the PDF list does not hold (676, 715, 729: its PDFs stop at roll call 476), and every 128th and 129th Senate vote (another layout). Member votes kept as printed with no line: 42 of 3,169 in the 128th-130th House: 21 a surname two seated members share (Fecteau, Foley and White in the 128th; Foley in the 129th), 11 a surname our roster lacks (Casas, 128th; Roberts-Lovell, 129th: Open States calls her Tiffany Roberts), and 10 a printed initial no seated member has (MillettH, 130th: Open States names H. Sawin Millett "Sawin Millett"). Compared with the dump: 93 of the 95 have a dump copy (131st House LD 2224, roll calls 515 and 516, have two dump copies with one tally, left unsettled); 9,603 member votes compared, 6 differ, all paired senators (131st Senate 759 and 760): the PDF prints a pair as not voting, the dump as the way each would have voted, and adds them to its tally, which is why those 2 tallies differ by the pair. 14 dump labels fit no record name: the two Pierces of the 128th (the dump gives neither a town; 8 votes, each lines up with Jeffrey K. Pierce as Dresden and Teresa Pierce as Falmouth) and ROBERTS of South Berwick against the kept Roberts-Lovell (6, all agreeing). Planted control: one 128th vote flipped in a copy of the record showed as the 7th difference.

Older Senates and roster names, 2026-11-21: the same dry batch read again. Floor roll calls read: 101, up from 95 (129th Senate 6, new; everything else as before). The 129th Senate's 6 votes all read and compare with the dump: 210 member votes, 0 differ (the dump writes the two Sanborns "SANBORN, H." and "SANBORN, L."; the comparison now reads that initial). Not read: 3 Senate votes of the 128th and 11 of the 130th, each a list row that links only a /LawMakerWeb page (robots.txt), now reported per vote; and the same 3 House votes of the 128th with no PDF. Member votes kept as printed with no line: 21 of 3,169 in the 128th-130th House, all a surname two seated members share (Fecteau, Foley, White), down from 42: Casás (128th; the extract spells him "CasÃ¡s", now put back), Roberts-Lovell (129th) and MillettH (130th) are named. In the 129th Senate, 6 ("Mr. President": the page names the office, not the person). Compared with the dump: 99 of the 101 have a dump copy; 9,819 member votes compared, 6 differ, the same paired 131st senators. 8 dump labels fit no record name, all the two Pierces of the 128th. Planted control: one 129th Senate vote flipped in a copy of the record showed as a 7th difference. A separate 11-bill sample of the 130th (LD 1, 2, 61, 102, 151, 220, 811, 1352, 1708, 1919, 1942) read 21 floor roll calls, 5 of them Senate, with none refused; 2,386 member votes compared, 2 differ, both a paired senator (130th roll call 807).

votes.floor_rule: A vote on the bill or on its Majority report is cited as its roll-call PDF on legislature.maine.gov, with the LD after a #. House: /house/Repository/Documents/<131>/RollCalls/<day>.<roll call>.<131R2>.pdf#LD2224 (the day's number, the roll call's number, the Legislature and session) from the 130th; the 129th's file is <day>.<roll call>.pdf and the 128th's the roll call alone (00245.pdf). Senate: /uploads/visual_edit/roll-call-<n>[-ld-<n>].pdf#LD1126 (the 129th's first files rc-<n>.pdf). The House PDF prints the Legislature, session, roll call number, the question, the LD and the day, then each member as "Surname, Initials" with Y, N or X in a column (X: absent or excused), and a tally (YES, NO, NV, EXC DAY, EXC VOTE, RES, VACANT). The 128th to 130th House PDFs print surnames only ("Austin, B." or "MartinJ" where two members share one): each is named from our Open States roster of that Legislature (backend/src/lib/maineLegislatureMembers.ts) as the one member of that family name seated on the vote's day, and with the initial's given name when one is printed. The Senate PDF prints the question and each senator's surname with an X under Yea, Nay, Abs or Exc, or a P for a senator paired with another (not counted in the tally, given no line); the saved member list of the vote's Legislature, from the Senate's senators pages (archived copies for the 128th to 131st), gives the full name. The live senators page is never read. The Senate PDF prints its own Legislature (the address names none), and the reader checks it fits the vote's date. The 129th and 130th print the presiding officer as "Mr. President" (kept as printed, no line) and a surname two senators share with an initial ("Sanborn H."); the 130th prints a pair as "P" and "P*" with a footnote naming both senators and how each would have voted, which must agree with the marks. Text order is not the order of the columns, so the reader pairs each mark with its member by x and y position. A vote is read only when the question is a vote on the bill (enactment, passage to be engrossed, final passage, a veto vote) or to accept the Majority report (Ought to Pass, as amended or not, or Ought Not to Pass), the LD and the Legislature in the PDF are the address's, the column heads are where the layout puts them, every member has one mark, each group holds the count the tally prints, every pair is one Yea and one Nay, and no two members render as one name. A surname the roster or member list does not fit to one member (two seated members share it, none has it, or two labels fit one member) is kept as printed and gives no line; the fetch prints how many. The Speaker is printed as "Mr. Speaker" or "Madam Speaker" and gets no line.
gaps: Floor votes on the bill and votes to accept the Majority report are read (runner, 2026-11-20). Maine's committees report out every bill, so accepting the Majority Ought Not to Pass report kills it with no later vote: that vote's Yea is a vote AGAINST the bill. The finding keeps act yea (the record's word) and carries against_bill: true; the bill table reads it as a No, and the coder prompt says how to read it. Measured 2017-2026: a member's vote to accept the Majority Ought to Pass report agreed with their next vote on the bill 96.8% of the time (16,852 pairs), against 94.6% for two successive votes on the bill.

A Minority report, a lettered report (Report "A", "B", "C" when a committee splits three ways), a report accepted unanimously, and votes to refer, table, indefinitely postpone, reconsider, recede or insist are motions and are not mapped. In the dry batch these left 12 bills with no floor vote read. Lettered reports agreed with the next vote on the bill 86.7% (Ought to Pass) and 31.6% (Ought Not to Pass, 3 votes) of the time, Minority reports 78-87%.
Absent, excused and "restricted from voting" are recorded as the record lists them, never as a Yea or a Nay; they seat no one.

The 128th to 130th House PDFs print surnames only. A surname two members seated that day share, one our roster lacks, or a printed initial no seated member has is kept as printed and gives no line: 21 of 3,169 member votes in the dry batch, all shared (Fecteau, Foley, White). Our roster is Open States' memberships, whose dates are sometimes blank (a blank counts as seated, so a surname is refused rather than guessed). Where the PDF prints a name Open States lacks, the House's own member profile of the time supplies it as an alternate name (Tiffany Roberts-Lovell, H. Sawin Millett Jr.; scripts/stage5/openstates/me-member-lists.ts).

The Senate PDF prints surnames only; the reader takes full names from the saved member list of the vote's Legislature (128th to 132nd, in backend/src/lib/maineLegislatureMembers.ts, rebuilt by scripts/stage5/openstates/me-member-lists.ts). The 133rd, seated in December 2026, needs its list added before its Senate votes read. The 128th's Senate list links every row (735) only to a /LawMakerWeb page, and the 130th's links 840 of 862 rows that way: those votes are reported as not read, never opened. The Legislative Record (lldc.mainelegislature.org/Open/LegRec/<128>/House|Senate/, one PDF per chamber per day, no robots.txt) prints each roll call's YEA and NAY names in two text columns and could fill them, with a reader of its own. The President's own vote in the 129th and 130th ("Mr. President") gives no line.

The 128th's House PDF list stops at roll call 476 (751 roll calls on its list): the 275 later 128th House votes have no PDF and are not read (3 in the dry batch); the Legislative Record prints them (see above). A senator paired with another is listed as paired, not as a Yea or a Nay, and gives no line (6 in the dry batch).
The Speaker's own vote (6 in the dry batch) gives no line: the PDF prints the office, not the name.

The House roll-call list links its rows to /LawMakerWeb pages on www.mainelegislature.org, which robots.txt disallows: those links are never followed; the PDF links on the allowed path are read instead.
A paper with no LD (HP 899 in the dry batch) has no allowed bill page and is not scanned (me_bill_page_disallowed).

texts.note: Texts are PDFs at /legis/bills/getPDF.asp?paper=<HP0001>&item=<n>&snum=<132>, served over https (https_texts). They print line numbers inline and the sponsors on page 1 ("Presented by Representative ... Cosponsored by ..."). How amendments mark new and deleted words was not read.

search_note: Maine sponsorships for 2017 to 2026 and House floor votes on the bill and on its Majority report for the 128th to 132nd Legislature, and Senate ones for the 129th to 132nd, come from the bill data on disk, checked against the Legislature's own roll-call PDFs: skip the Legislature's roll-call lists and PDFs, and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". 128th Senate votes are not read, and most 130th Senate votes are not (their list links no PDF): the bill's report names each one not read; search those as usual. Never open a /LawMakerWeb page (robots.txt). Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, 429, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- Maine bills are Legislative Documents (LD) numbered through the whole two-year Legislature; the paper number (HP, SP) names the chamber a bill starts in.
- Floor votes kept: enactment, passage to be engrossed, final passage, a veto vote, and the vote to accept the Majority report. A Yea to accept the Majority Ought Not to Pass report is a vote against the bill (the finding carries against_bill). Minority and lettered reports and other motions are skipped.
- Texts: the marks for new and deleted words were not checked.
quirks: robots.txt on legislature.maine.gov disallows /LawMakerWeb and /legis/LawMakerWeb only; the roll-call lists and PDFs are on allowed paths. robots.txt on www.mainelegislature.org disallows /LawMakerWeb and blocks several named AI crawlers entirely; the verifier's user agent is not among them, and the texts (/legis/bills/getPDF.asp) are on an allowed path.
One House roll-call page in the disallowed /LawMakerWeb path was fetched by mistake on 2026-11-20 and deleted unread; nothing from it was used.
The 132nd House PDFs print "Collins, A. C" (no stop after the last initial) on every roll call; the label rule allows it.
The House record prints "OHalloran, D.L." without the apostrophe; the label fit ignores apostrophes in a family name.

The Senate list on the Legislature's site splits rows by paragraph, by a bill-title block, and sometimes holds two roll calls in one paragraph (131st #304 and #305); one roll call can have two PDF links (#31), and a file number can differ from the roll call's (#107 in file 108). The fetch splits each row at the next roll call's link, checks every PDF on the page falls in a row, and skips a file already read.

No crawl delay is stated; the fetch waits 1 second between requests. No 403, 429 or bot check was met. The line tool wrote 709 lines in 9.7 seconds from an empty page cache (7 PDFs and the senators page): under 3 seconds per 200 votes.
The store's one Maine instrument, ME-LD-652-2015 (127th Legislature), is older than the converted sessions (128th on), so the scan cannot find it.

The 131st Senate PDFs store words and numbers in pieces ("YEA: 1" then "6"; "Question" ": E" "nactment"; "M" "otion"), and a veto vote prints "Motion: Reconsideration - Veto" and "(Veto Sustained)" above the column heads. A pair prints a P under Yea and one under Nay with the pair's number above (roll call 760), or, for one pair, "P" and "P*" with no number (759).

The 128th House PDF lays its tally out otherwise ("YES: 122 NO: 24 ABSENT: 4", then "EXCUSED: 1" and a sentence naming the excused member), prints no vacant seats, and sometimes stores a close mark with its label ("X Lockman"). The 129th has one roll call with two PDFs (038.089.pdf and 038.089V.pdf): neither is read.

Earlier Legislatures' senators pages were read from Internet Archive copies (web.archive.org, the raw "id_" form), two per Legislature where they exist, and merged; every source is listed beside its list.

The 130th Senate PDFs print "130th LEGISLATURE" and "MOTION: ENACTMENT" in capitals, store a pair's star apart from its P, and name the presiding officer "Mr. President"; the 129th spells the session out ("First Regular Session"), curls the amendment's quotes (Committee Amendment “A”), and may write "Excused." or an initial in the footer ("Senator Sanborn L. excused."). A 130th House veto vote prints "ROLL CALL NO. 448V". The 128th's Senate list is typed by hand ("Roll Call Number 299", "Roll Call number 322", "Roll Call Number #676") with two links broken ("rhttp://legislature..."). Open States' 2026-11 extract double-encodes one name ("CasÃ¡s"); the roster builder puts it back.
